title: Store results in subfolders by date
description:
Currently, we store all the test result `.json` files in a flat folder in the `__test-results` folder in the `_test-results` branch:

``` r
files <- gh::gh(
  "GET /repos/:owner/:repo/contents/__test_results",
  owner = "rstudio",
  repo = "shinycoreci",
  ref = "_test_results",
  .limit = Inf
)

length(files)
#> [1] 1000
files |> purrr::map_chr("name") |> sort() |> head()
#> [1] "gha-01830f4-2023_06_08_05_04-3.6-Linux.json"
#> [2] "gha-01830f4-2023_06_08_05_04-4.0-Linux.json"
#> [3] "gha-01830f4-2023_06_08_05_04-4.1-Linux.json"
#> [4] "gha-01830f4-2023_06_08_05_04-4.2-Linux.json"
#> [5] "gha-01830f4-2023_06_08_05_04-4.3-Linux.json"
#> [6] "gha-01830f4-2023_06_08_05_37-3.6-macOS.json"
```

As the above reprex shows, the GitHub REST API won't list more than 1,000 files at a time, so we can't programmatically get a subset of the results. 

Similarly, `git sparse-checkout` runs into the same problem as it wants to limit checked-out files by subfolder:

```bash
# start in a temp location
git clone --no-checkout --filter=blob:none https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci -b _test-results
cd shinycoreci
git sparse-checkout init --cone
git sparse-checkout set __test-results
git checkout
```

The above doesn't help because we're still needing to checkout **all** of the test results files. If they were in subfolders, both of the above would work

```r
gh::gh(
  "GET /repos/:owner/:repo/contents/__test_results/2025/01",
  owner = "rstudio",
  repo = "shinycoreci",
  ref = "_test_results",
  .limit = Inf
)
```

```bash
# start in a temp location
git clone --no-checkout --filter=blob:none https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci -b _test-results
cd shinycoreci
git sparse-checkout init --cone
git sparse-checkout set __test-results/2025/01
git checkout
```

Also, doing a shallow depth clone is slow and pulls a huge amount of data:

```r
tmpdir <- tempfile("shinycoreci-test-results-")

processx::run(
  "git",
  args = c(
    "clone",
    "--depth", 
    "1",
    "https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci.git",
    "-b", 
    "_test_results",
    tmpdir
  ),
  echo = TRUE,
  echo_cmd = TRUE
)
```
```r
test_results <- fs::path(tmpdir, "__test_results")
test_results |> fs::dir_ls() |> length()
#> [1] 8873
test_results |> fs::dir_ls() |> fs::file_info() |> getElement("size") |> sum()
#> 4.5G
```

title: Package updates shouldn't cause test failures unless behavior changes
description:
There are more than a few places where we have embedded package versions into our tests, which means that package updates for key packages can cause our tests to fail. Two recent examples:

* #247 
* #248

There may be a path forward in adding a `compare=` function as an argument to `app$expect_values()`, similar to the `compare` argument of `app$expect_screenshot()` (added in rstudio/shinytest2#231). We could have a function, e.g. `shinycoreci::compare_json_ignore_pkg_versions()` that would strip package versions before comparing.

There's enough tooling around tests that this isn't a blocker, but I find the "mytest" context a bit weird in our tests. I'd much rather we have `test-026-shiny-inline.R` than `test-mytest.R` in `inst/apps/026-shiny-inline/tests/testthat/`.

title: Don't use `variant` if only saving a single screenshot
description:
In several cases, in particular with focused tests that don't primarily rely on snapshots, we only take screenshots on a single OS and R version, e.g. MacOS + r-latest.

In these cases, we should set `variant = NULL` in the app options.

We should also have shared code that returns `TRUE` for `mac-latest + r-latest`, to facilitate deciding whether or not to take a screenshot.

As a side benefit, this also helps with the initial set up of a test; the first screenshots can be created locally regardless of OS and R version.

title: Allow shared code based on {staticimports}
description:
We occasionally need utility functions and shared code between apps, but we don't want to introduce a dependency on shinycoreci in the test code. Ideally, testing apps should be completely isolated.

We could build on [staticimports](https://github.com/wch/staticimports) to store shared code in `{shinycoreci}/inst/staticexports` that is then "vendored" into the test app folders.

We'd also need a shinycoreci function that walks the test apps and can update any out-of-date imports.

title: Review and optimize the test apps and tests
description:
Some of our shinycoreci test results has been flaky due to the trivial snapshot differences

We probably need to review our existing test-apps and shinytest2 tests as a team and see if flaky tests or duplicate test apps be removed

Usually from my past reviews of the test failures and reviewing them via `fix_all_snaps`, the case was that the tests were failing mostly due to pixel differences in the snapshots. There was an improvement with the shinytest to shinytest2, but we still have the problem.

It would be good to review the test results for ex: check the dashboard results https://rstudio.github.io/shinycoreci/results/2022/10/20/ and 

- [ ] Understand why the tests are failing (dependency changes?, snapshot differences?, other?)
- [ ] Can these be fixed? If so, would they be stable?
- [ ] Understand if all the test apps are needed in shinycoreci and the daily test run. Right now, we have around ~150 apps covering specific RShiny features (https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/tree/main/inst/apps)
- [ ] Can we optimize few test apps in to one test app? Repeating the same process for another set
- [ ] Goal is to have maintainable and optimized number of tests

cc: @jcheng5 @shalutiwari @cpsievert @schloerke

title: Implement `fix_snaps()`
description:
Problem:

How to look at `_snaps` differences from a different branches of the same `_snaps` folder.

Problematic behavior: 
* Changed files are named differently. (Add the `.new` file extension)
* New files that have no original file are automatically added. (No `.new` extension will exist)
* Deleted files are missing. No information to state that they are removed.

This makes it difficult without reinventing the `git` wheel.



Ideas...

### `gha-` branches
* Commits can be a single commit of all changes found during GHA run. (Current behavior)


### Behavior for `shinycoreci::fix_snaps()`

1. Validate there are no `.new` `_snaps` files locally
1. For each `gha-` branch 
	1. Auto accept all snaps that have a `.new` file
	1. Count changes for each branch / app
1. Display diagnostics of counts of mac/win/ubuntu failures in the console
1. Be able to choose which branches are looked at
	* Default: All
1. Be able to choose which apps are looked at
	* Default: All
1. For each selected `gha-` branch
	1. Checkout branch
	2. Create patch file from changes in branch
1. Checkout _main_ branch
1. For each patch file
	4. Apply changes in patch: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-apply . (Does not commit changes)
	1. If any Apps were selected
		1. `unstage` / `git checkout -- .` all app folders that do not match requested Apps
* (DONE)

* User uses `GitHub Desktop` to accept or reject the changes


### Benefits of auto accepting and applying patches of the `gha-` branches

* Can perform a single commit back to the repo when done
* Use GitHub desktop to quickly look at apps. 
	* Faster than `{diffviewer}`. 
	* Can perform sweeping "discard" changes
* GitHub Desktop will look at files that are the same file name
	* New files will be "added"
	* Deleted files will be "deleted"
	* Changed files will be "modified"
* ... If auto-accepting is not done,
 	* New files will be "added"
	* Deleted files will be "deleted"
	* Changed files will be an "added" file with a similar name (`FILE.new.EXT`). **Hard to see differences!!**

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
Cc @schloerke

The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: entire_lizard*

```
  - 022-unicode-chinese : mytest

  - 203-flexdashboard-biclustering : mytest
  - 205-dynamic-tabs-compat : cosmo4 

Select the Git branches you'd like to use 

1: (All branches)
2: gha-6fc6549-2021_03_18_20_31-4.0-Linux
3: gha-6fc6549-2021_03_18_20_31-3.6-macOS
4: gha-6fc6549-2021_03_18_20_25-4.0-macOS
5: gha-6fc6549-2021_03_18_20_30-4.0-Windows

Selection: 
```

New request: When inspecting the apps, It would be helpful to have the list of apps (with the branches that specific app failed) for the shinytest results. Similar to below

```
*  022-unicode-chinese : mytest - 4.0-Windows, 4.0-mac, 3.4-Linux
*  200-flexdashboard-render-text : mytest - 4.0-Windows, 4.0-mac, 3.4-Linux
*  201-flexdashboard-render-text : mytest - 4.0-Windows, 4.0-mac, 3.4-Linux

Select the app you'd like to use 

1: (All branches)
2: 022-unicode-chinese : mytest
3: 200-flexdashboard-render-text : mytest
4: 201-flexdashboard-render-text : mytest
```

Default branches to test all branches. But have it possible to select the branch

Above format gives us the opportunity to understand the holistic view of all branches/OS/R version a specific app failed. Also,  in the selection option, we should be able to select a specific (or a new) app test if fails (vs branch) and just view the test results of that app which saves time. Choosing the branch with set of apps failed in that branch sometime results in redundant review of test failures.

title: Issue with finding multiple current folders with in an app
description:
With apps like `301-bs-themes`  and `302-bootswatch-themes`, we test the app with multiple bootswatch themes. That means when `fix_all_gha_branches()` is run, a current folder is created for every theme.

https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci-apps/tree/master/apps/301-bs-themes/tests/shinytest
https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci-apps/tree/master/apps/302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest

After the `fix_all_gha_branches()` is complete, not all the current folders are deleted. Here are some of the logs I noticed.

```
......
......
Switched to branch 'gha-80b39ba-2021_02_18_08_39-4.0-macOS'
Error in validate_no_unexpected_shinytest_folders(dir) : 
  There should be no *-current folders. Found: 
* 301-bs-themes/tests/shinytest/custom4-current
* 301-bs-themes/tests/shinytest/default3-current
* 301-bs-themes/tests/shinytest/default4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/cerulean4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/cosmo3-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/cosmo4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/cyborg3-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/cyborg4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/darkly3-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/darkly4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/flatly3-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/flatly4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/journal3-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/journal4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/litera4-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/lumen3-current
* 302-bootswatch-themes/tests/shinytest/lumen4-current
* 302-bootswat
git checkout master
Switched to branch 'master'
```

We have to find a way to find all the current folders and delete them inorder to be able to push the gha commits.
